newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - DEC 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS - DEC 10.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:
KATHIMERINI

--The fire from strikers comes hard and fast as an announcement from the national economy and finance ministry reiterates that there are no margins for hand-outs. Similar announcements are expected to come out of today's Cabinet meeting on the civil servants' uniform pay scale and the farmers' protests.

--The majority of private investments approved for subsidies last year face cancellation following delays in implementation. Development Minister Vasso Papandreou tells businessmen that unjustified delays will mean automatic exclusion.

--The deadline for clearing transactions at the stock exchange will be extended from 48 to 72 hours, sources say National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou has decided, following appeals from all bourse bodies.
--Insurance agents appeal to the development ministry to take action over a specific insurance company which has ceased to issue receipts and to pay compensation.
IMERISIA

--Greece's Public Power Company's (DEH) board is due to approve the implementation of a new tariff scale for industries and business at its meeting today. The new scale will provide cheaper power at differing times of the day, including peak consumption times.

--The government has decided to put the profit-making "Duty Free" chain of stores on the stock exchange with a share offer of between 10-20 percent. Demand will determine whether the share offer is enlarged. Duty Free has a turnover of close to 40 billion drachmas and profits of over 12 billion.
KERDOS

--The last restrictions on the movement of capital will be lifted by the end of 1997, with the extension of the right to Greek residents to open accounts in foreign exchange, according to the deputy governor of the Bank of Greece.
--As the farmers' blockade enters its 13th day, industry and commercial enterprises have reached the limits of despair, with enormous problems facing export firms in the clothing and food sector.
--More than 100 development ministry and prefectural employees have begun market checks to avert possible profiteering on prices in the light of the continuing farmers' blockade.
--The audit on Athens bourse members has entered its final stage with the cross-referencing of bourse clients.
--The finance ministry is concerned that the blockade will have a negative effect on the collection of revenues for the current month as well as the next two months.
EXPRESS
--The government is examining the details of how to settle farmers' debts of 350 billion drachmas but will not proceed to dialogue while 'hostage' to the farmers, sources say.

--Possible mergers in the banking system which will make the sector more competitive was the major focus of concern at the Hellenic-American Chamber of Commerce and Union of Greek Banks congress which began yesterday. National Bank Governor Theodoros Karatzas said he was in favour of mergers and buyouts that would act to reduced operating costs.
NAFTEMBORIKI
--The Cabinet meeting today is expected to support Prime Minister Costas Simitis's stance last week that the government will not back down on the farmers' demands.
--The wholesale price index is on a positive course, according to the National Statistics Sevice, meaning good prospects for the consumer price index.

--A 370 million ECU loan is expected to be approved today for the construction of the Rio-Antirrio bridge, a project that will link the road networks of the Peloponese with northwest and central Greece. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
